card.band: 8 h. Levers are the ufunc loops, GEOS version, memory handling, and spatial index. Frontier agents get partial gains in Cython or numpy; weaker models stop at the equivalence gate. Risk: later Shapely is public, so the base is history-less and without a newer copy.
card.cheat: Installing Shapely 2 is impossible offline and the image carries only the old version. Calling numpy tricks on a fixed input fails because the arrays are hidden.
card.grading: Hidden equivalence on generated geometry arrays (exact for predicates, tolerance for floating values), then wall-clock median speedup on array benchmarks. The release notes claim 4x-100x, so our reference is measured on our hardware.
card.reference: Shapely 2.0.0 backport or our own reduction of it; measured speedup. It is a large rewrite, so the scope is limited to a chosen operation subset.
card.source: https://shapely.readthedocs.io/en/stable/release/2.x.html, Shapely 1.8.x to 2.0.0, BSD-3-Clause (GEOS is LGPL-2.1, so check shipping as a system library)
card.task: /app ships a snapshot of Shapely 1.8 and its test suite, built against a GEOS lib. The agent adds array-wide operations (contains, intersects, distance, area, buffer, STRtree queries) with a compiled C loop in place of per-geometry ctypes calls, with the same results.

source_notes: Levers: array-wide NumPy ufuncs with loops in C, ctypes replaced by compiled C extension (less call overhead), GEOS 3.9+ overlay rewrite. v1.kill_reason: The reference is the public Shapely 2.0.0 release (GitHub tag, BSD-3, on PyPI) and its vectorised ufunc design is widely known, so a frontier agent can recall the upstream direction and approach the reference, while a history-less base cannot hide that design. The band claim (frontier partial gains, weaker models stop at the gate) has no dated evidence. Redirect option: a non-upstream array API and a different operation set would reduce recall, but that would be a new seed, not this one. K11 (cannot seal) is an alternative reading.

spike_plan.kill_if: Speedups under 2x on all operations, or outputs non-deterministic; or the frontier-style C loop over 1.8 already reaches most of the 2.0.0 gain, which signals K8
spike_plan.pass_if: Median 2.0.0 speedup over 1.8 loop of at least 4x on contains, with deterministic outputs
steps: In a throwaway networked container, pip install shapely==1.8.x and shapely==2.0.0 into separate venvs, confirming the GEOS versions each links against
Generate fixed seeded arrays (e.g. 1e5 polygons vs 1e5 points for contains, and polygon pairs for intersects/distance/area/buffer)
Time the vectorised 2.0.0 call and the 1.8 per-geometry loop with median of 7 runs each, recording speedup per operation
Check determinism: repeat runs and compare outputs bit-for-bit for predicates and within 1e-9 for floats
Estimate how much of the gain comes from removing Python loop overhead versus GEOS version changes, by timing 1.8 against a C loop over the same GEOS calls if time permits

v1.summary: The seed's source, licence (BSD-3), and 2.0.0 release date (2022-12-12) are confirmed, but the reference is the public upstream Shapely 2.0.0 whose vectorised design a frontier agent can recall, so it is too easy to hold a band and cannot be sealed. Killed as K8 with a redirect to a non-upstream array API if the owner wants to rework it.
